priorStories.headline: US consumer prices rose 0.4% in October
priorStories.body:
The Consumer Price Index increased 0.4% in October after a 0.6% rise in September, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported Tuesday. Those monthly figures are seasonally adjusted. Prices excluding food and energy rose 0.3%; food rose 0.5%, energy 0.7% and shelter 0.3%.

BLS could not publish most year-over-year comparisons because the October 2025 government shutdown had prevented collection of the necessary survey data.

candidates.summary: Russian and Ukrainian delegations began a second day of US-brokered negotiations in Abu Dhabi on November 11. Ukraine’s delegation leader Rustem Umerov confirmed that negotiations had resumed. The talks were mediated by US envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner. No agreement or breakthrough was reported in the available account.
candidates.title: Russia and Ukraine resume US-brokered talks in Abu Dhabi
candidates.geography: United Arab Emirates; Ukraine; Russia; United States

candidates.summary: Germany’s Federal Cartel Office said on November 11 that PayPal’s prohibition on merchants charging customers extra for using its payment service may restrict competition and violate the law. The authority described its findings as preliminary and gave PayPal an opportunity to respond. It is also considering recovery of profits attributable to the practice. PayPal disputed the preliminary assessment and said it would continue engaging with the proceedings.
candidates.title: German competition authority issues preliminary findings on PayPal merchant rules

candidates.summary: Russia and Ukraine agreed in principle to a large prisoner-of-war exchange as two days of US-mediated talks concluded in Abu Dhabi on November 11. Delegation leaders Vladimir Medinsky and Rustem Umerov confirmed the planned exchange. US envoy Jared Kushner said the numbers remained to be finalized. No exchange had yet occurred, and the talks produced no major breakthrough on ending the war.
candidates.title: Russia and Ukraine agree in principle to prisoner exchange as Abu Dhabi talks conclude
candidates.geography: United Arab Emirates; Ukraine; Russia; United States

candidates.summary: Workers across Spain staged a general strike on November 11 over housing affordability, backed by the UGT and CCOO unions and tenants' associations. Unions reported four million participants; that figure was their estimate. Reuters reported uneven participation, with stronger support in coastal regions, and shops closing in Madrid and Barcelona. It was Spain's first general strike since 2012.
candidates.title: Spain holds general strike over housing affordability

candidates.summary: Spain's data protection authority AEPD said on November 11 that it had opened an investigation into alleged child sexual abuse material on TikTok following reporting by Maldita.es. It rejected the government's request to temporarily block the entire platform, instead considering measures against specific unlawful content after obtaining information from TikTok and Maldita.es. Spain's attorney general separately ordered a cybercrime investigation. TikTok did not immediately respond to Reuters' request for comment.
candidates.title: Spanish privacy watchdog opens TikTok investigation without ordering platform-wide block

candidates.summary: Addressing the COP31 Leaders' Summit in Antalya on November 11, UN Secretary-General António Guterres proposed a Climate Justice Compact covering a faster transition away from fossil fuels, protection for vulnerable communities, climate finance and international cooperation. He urged developed countries to deliver at least $300 billion annually by 2035 and establish milestones for tripling adaptation finance. These were calls for action, not a newly adopted agreement.
candidates.title: Guterres proposes Climate Justice Compact at COP31 leaders' summit

sources.name: UN Framework Convention on Climate Change

candidates.summary: WMO and UNDRR released their Global Status of Multi-Hazard Early Warning Systems 2026 report on November 11, coinciding with a high-level event in Antalya. It found that 136 countries, or 70 percent, reported some multi-hazard early warning capability, an increase of 17 countries from March 2025. Small island developing states had the lowest reported coverage, while least developed countries had the lowest overall comprehensiveness scores.
candidates.title: UN report finds early warning capability in 136 countries, with major coverage gaps

candidates.summary: AWS announced general availability of AWS Emulator on November 11. The local software lets developers and coding agents test applications using AWS APIs, SDKs and command-line tools without provisioning cloud resources for the emulated operations. AWS said the emulator has no additional service fee and its source is available on GitHub. The company cautioned that it does not evaluate identity and resource policies as AWS does and should not replace security testing or final application testing on AWS.
candidates.title: AWS releases local emulator for testing cloud applications

candidates.summary: Representative Robert Garcia responded on November 11 to a warning from White House counsel Will Scharf about planned congressional investigations. Scharf's November 10 letter argued that investigations must serve a legislative purpose and warned that abusive subpoenas or intimidation could warrant investigation. Garcia said Congress derives its oversight authority from the Constitution rather than White House permission and would not be deterred. The exchange concerned prospective oversight after Democrats take control of Congress; it did not establish that any investigation or subpoena was unlawful.
candidates.title: Garcia rejects White House warning over planned congressional oversight

candidates.summary: Two people were killed and 17 others injured, four critically, when a three-story mixed-use building in Brooklyn's Flatbush neighborhood partially collapsed on November 11, according to officials. Firefighters rescued people from the rubble during the evening and continued searching into the night. The cause remained under investigation. City buildings commissioner Ahmed Tigani said excavation was underway at an adjacent construction site when the building fell.
candidates.title: Brooklyn building collapse kills two; rescue operations continue into night

candidates.summary: The ocean liner SS United States was deliberately sunk off Florida's Panhandle on November 11 to become the world's largest artificial reef. The hourslong operation concluded in the evening. Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution announced a multiyear research effort to monitor water chemistry, microbial activity and biological colonization around the newly deployed structure. The sinking was part of an Okaloosa County project intended to create marine habitat and support diving and fishing.
candidates.title: SS United States sunk off Florida to create artificial reef and research site

sources.name: Associated Press via NBC 6 South Florida

candidates.summary: Workers across Spain staged a general strike over housing affordability on November 11, backed by UGT, CCOO and tenants' associations. Unions estimated four million participants and described the strike as mostly peaceful, with uneven participation. Evening clashes occurred in Barcelona and Madrid; Reuters witnessed police using foam bullets, tear gas and pepper spray in Madrid. Police reported at least 73 arrests nationwide by 2100 GMT. Unions alleged a police operation injured 20 protesters and said they would file a complaint; the Interior Ministry did not immediately comment.
candidates.title: Spain housing strike draws millions by union estimate, with evening clashes and arrests
